transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been doing some things lately that don’t really feel like me. I don’t want to make it sound overly dramatic, but it’s started to scare me a little—like walking out in the middle of work deployments, or driving around really late at night with no plan. I’ve always handled stress pretty responsibly, so… this feels off, and I thought I should talk to someone before it gets worse.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

Yeah… I mean, a little. Maybe more than a little, if I’m being honest.

I used to kind of build my week around things—salsa, book club, yoga, having people over and cooking Guatemalan food. I really enjoyed that. Lately I’ll say I’m tired or something came up, and I cancel. Then I just sit at home scrolling on my phone or put on a show I’m not really watching.

It sounds bad when I say it out loud. I don’t know if that’s what you mean, but… yes, I’ve noticed that.
Have you noticed any periods where you felt unusually high, extremely irritable, or so energized that you didn’t need much sleep?

I don’t think so… not really. I mean, I have nights where I don’t sleep well, but I wouldn’t say I feel energized from it or unusually good.

I can get irritable, sure, but it feels more like being worn down than anything “high,” if that makes sense. I’m not staying up because I feel amazing or like I can take on the world. At least, I don’t think so.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating much less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Um… I don’t think there’s been a big change there. My appetite is maybe a little inconsistent, but I haven’t noticed, like, significant weight loss or anything like that.

I’m not tracking it super closely, so I don’t want to give you the wrong answer, but nothing has really stood out to me.
Have you noticed that you feel tired or low on energy most of the time, even when you haven’t been doing much?

Yeah… I guess I have. I mean, I still get through work and everything, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’m tired a lot.

Most nights I’m lying there replaying parts of what happened at the office, and then when I finally do fall asleep, I’ll wake up tense—from a dream or even just some little noise. So by the time I’m supposed to start the day, I already feel worn out. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling this way—losing interest in things, feeling tired, and having trouble sleeping—for at least two weeks straight?

Yeah… definitely more than two weeks. I wish it were just that.

It’s been going on since that late-night cutover incident at work… a little over a year ago now, maybe around 13 months. Some weeks are better than others, so I don’t want to overstate it, but it hasn’t really gone away.
Have you found yourself feeling like you’re a failure or that you’ve let people down, or been really hard on yourself about things lately?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to sit around thinking I’m a failure or anything, but I do get really hard on myself.

Even on quiet days, there’s this mix of fear and shame just kind of sitting in my chest. Like I should’ve handled things better, or done something differently… and then part of me feels like if I relax too much, something could still happen. I know that probably sounds a little dramatic, but that’s sort of how it feels.
Have you had episodes like this before, or is this the first time you’ve felt this way over an extended period?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I’ve had stressful periods before, like anyone, and I’ve been tired or down for a little while here and there… but I don’t know if I’d call them “episodes” like this.

This feels like the first time it’s gone on this long, at least that I can remember. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?
Have you ever had a period in the past where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble sleeping for more than a couple of weeks at a time?

I don’t think so… not really. I mean, I’ve had rough stretches before, sure, and maybe a few bad nights of sleep or feeling kind of low, but I don’t remember anything that lasted more than a couple weeks in that same way.

At least, not that stands out to me. Is that okay as an answer?
Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble sleeping for more than two weeks in a row, before this current period?

I don’t think so, no. Not before this. I mean, I’ve had normal stressful times and a few nights here and there where sleep wasn’t great, but I can’t really remember a stretch like that lasting more than two weeks in a row.

I hope that makes sense—I’m trying to answer it the way you mean.
Have you ever experienced a time in your life before this current period where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble sleeping for more than two weeks in a row?

I don’t think I have, no. I know I’ve said that a few ways, but before this I don’t really remember anything that was that sustained—like more than two weeks straight of feeling down or not sleeping well.

I’ve had normal ups and downs, but nothing that I would point to as the same kind of stretch. Is that the kind of answer you’re looking for?
Have you ever had a period in your life before this one where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble sleeping for more than two weeks in a row?

No, I really don’t think so. Before this period, I had stressful times like anyone, and maybe a bad week here or there, but I can’t think of anything that went on for more than two weeks straight like that.

I hope I’m not being repetitive—I just don’t remember a period like that before.
Have you ever had a time in your life before this current period where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble sleeping for more than two weeks in a row?

I’m sorry, I know you’ve asked it a few times. I don’t think so, not before this current period. I can remember ordinary stress or a rough few days, but not a solid stretch of more than two weeks where I was down or not interested in things or sleeping badly.

If I’m understanding the question right, then my answer would be no.
Have you had any periods of feeling down, losing interest in things, or having trouble sleeping that started after this current episode began but happened more than two weeks ago?

Yes… I think so. I mean, it’s not like I’m doing absolutely nothing, but I’ve definitely pulled back.

I used to kind of plan my week around things—salsa, book club, yoga, having people over and cooking Guatemalan food—and lately I mostly cancel or just don’t go. Then I end up at home scrolling on my phone or with a show on that I’m not really watching.

I don’t know if that counts the way you mean it, but it’s been more than just a couple days.
Have you ever had a time in your life before this current period when you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble sleeping for more than two weeks in a row?

I don’t think so, no. I’m trying to answer it the right way… before this current period, I can’t really point to a time where it lasted more than two weeks like that.

I mean, I had normal stress and off days, but nothing that I’d describe as a whole stretch of feeling down or losing interest or not sleeping for that long.

Have you ever had a period of feeling down, losing interest in things, or having trouble sleeping that lasted more than two weeks, occurred before this current episode, and was followed by at least two months where you felt back to your usual self?

No, I don’t think so. Before this current episode, I can’t really remember anything like that lasting more than two weeks and then having, you know, a clear couple of months after where I felt back to normal.

I had ups and downs like anyone, but not a distinct period like what you’re describing. Is that the kind of answer you’re looking for?

Have you ever had a time before this current episode where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble sleeping for more than two weeks in a row, and then after that time, you felt completely back to your usual self for at least two months?

I don’t think so… I know I’m kind of repeating myself, but before this current stretch, I can’t remember a time like that—more than two weeks and then clearly back to myself for a couple months.

There were stressful periods, sure, but nothing that stands out in the way you’re describing. Does that make sense?
